BiblicalUsage: Gasham means to shower violently, to pour down rain. It appears once, in Jeremiah 14:22, where the prophet asks whether any of the vanities of the Gentiles can cause rain, or whether the heavens can give showers. The answer is no — only the LORD our God makes all these things.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the showers belong to God alone; the idols of the nations cannot make it rain, and I hold that the God who sends the showers is the only God worth waiting on.
